t: You're looking at the statue of Beau Brummell, outside the southern entrance of Piccadilly Arcade on Jermyn Street in St James's. It's by the Czech sculptor Irena Sedlecká. Brummell was an English socialite who shaped men's fashion in the Regency era, and he was a close friend of the Prince Regent, the future George the Fourth. They quarrelled, and with debts mounting he took refuge in France. He died in Caen. It's fitting that he's remembered here, among the shops of one of London's great streets for men's style.
